sanskrit: taṃ hīnaparṇaṃ patitāgraśākhaṃ; viśīrṇapuṣpaṃ prasamīkṣya vāyuḥ uvāca vākyaṃ smayamāna enaṃ; mudā yutaṃ śalmaliṃ rugṇaśākham
english: Beholding it stripped of its leaves, its topmost branches fallen, its blossoms scattered, the Wind spoke this word, smiling, to the silk-cotton tree, its boughs now broken, that had once stood there flush with joy:

sanskrit: aham apy evam eva tvāṃ kurvāṇaḥ śalmale ruṣā ātmanā yat kṛtaṃ kṛtsnaṃ śākhānām apakarṣaṇam
english: "I too, O silk-cotton tree, would have done to you in my wrath exactly this — the wholesale stripping away of your branches that you have now wrought upon yourself."

sanskrit: hīnapuṣpāgraśākhas tvaṃ śīrṇāṅkurapalāśavān ātmadurmantriteneha madvīryavaśago 'bhavaḥ
english: "Bereft now of blossoms and topmost boughs, your buds and foliage withered, by your own ill counsel you have here fallen under the sway of my might."

sanskrit: etac chrutvā vaco vāyoḥ śalmalir vrīḍitas tadā atapyata vacaḥ smṛtvā nārado yat tadābravīt
english: Hearing this speech of the Wind, the silk-cotton tree was then put to shame and tormented with regret, recalling the words that Nārada had once spoken to it.

sanskrit: evaṃ yo rājaśārdūla durbalaḥ san balīyasā vairam āsajjate bālas tapyate śalmalir yathā
english: Thus, O tiger among kings, the fool who, being weak, fastens enmity upon one stronger than himself comes to grief, even as the silk-cotton tree did.

sanskrit: tasmād vairaṃ na kurvīta durbalo balavattaraiḥ śoced dhi vairaṃ kurvāṇo yathā vai śalmalis tathā
english: Therefore let the weak man form no enmity with those of greater strength; for one who provokes such enmity will surely grieve, just as the silk-cotton tree grieved.

sanskrit: na hi vairaṃ mahātmāno vivṛṇvanty apakāriṣu śanaiḥ śanair mahārāja darśayanti sma te balam
english: For the great-souled do not openly proclaim their enmity against those who wrong them; rather, O great king, little by little they reveal their power.

sanskrit: vairaṃ na kurvīta naro durbuddhir buddhijīvinā buddhir buddhimato yāti tūleṣv iva hutāśanaḥ
english: Let not the dull-witted man pick a quarrel with one who lives by his wits; the intellect of the wise man advances upon him as fire advances through cotton.

sanskrit: na hi buddhyā samaṃ kiṃ cid vidyate puruṣe nṛpa tathā balena rājendra na samo 'stīti cintayet
english: Nothing in a man, O king, is found to equal intellect; nor, O lord of kings, should one imagine that anything equals strength.

sanskrit: tasmāt kṣameta bālāya jaḍāya badhirāya ca balādhikāya rājendra tad dṛṣṭaṃ tvayi śatruhan
english: Therefore, O lord of kings, one should bear with the foolish, the dull, the deaf, and even with one of superior strength; that, O slayer of foes, has been seen in you.

sanskrit: akṣauhiṇyo daśaikā ca sapta caiva mahādyute balena na samā rājann arjunasya mahātmanaḥ
english: Eleven akṣauhiṇīs, O you of great splendour, together with seven more, were not, O king, a match in strength for the great-souled Arjuna.

sanskrit: hatās tāś caiva bhagnāś ca pāṇḍavena yaśasvinā caratā balam āsthāya pākaśāsaninā mṛdhe
english: And they were slain and shattered by the illustrious son of Pāṇḍu, the son of Indra, slayer of Pāka's foe, as he ranged the field relying upon his might in battle.

sanskrit: uktās te rājadharmāś ca āpaddharmāś ca bhārata vistareṇa mahārāja kiṃ bhūyaḥ prabravīmi te
english: The duties of kings and the duties for times of distress have been told you at length, O Bhārata; what more, O great king, shall I declare to you?

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca pāpasya yad adhiṣṭhānaṃ yataḥ pāpaṃ pravartate etad icchāmy ahaṃ jñātuṃ tattvena bharatarṣabha
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: That which is the seat of sin, the source from which sin springs forth — this I wish to know in its very truth, O bull of the Bharatas.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca pāpasya yad adhiṣṭhānaṃ tac chṛṇuṣva narādhipa eko lobho mahāgrāho lobhāt pāpaṃ pravartate
english: Bhīṣma said: Hear, O ruler of men, what the seat of sin is. Greed alone is the great devourer; from greed all sin proceeds.

sanskrit: ataḥ pāpam adharmaś ca tathā duḥkham anuttamam nikṛtyā mūlam etad dhi yena pāpakṛto janāḥ
english: From it come sin and unrighteousness and unsurpassed sorrow; this indeed is, through deceit, the very root whereby men become workers of evil.

sanskrit: lobhāt krodhaḥ prabhavati lobhāt kāmaḥ pravartate lobhān mohaś ca māyā ca mānastambhaḥ parāsutā
english: From greed arises wrath; from greed desire is set in motion; from greed come delusion and guile, arrogant pride, and the destruction of others' lives.

sanskrit: akṣamā hrīparityāgaḥ śrīnāśo dharmasaṃkṣayaḥ abhidhyāprajñatā caiva sarvaṃ lobhāt pravartate
english: Intolerance, the casting off of shame, the loss of prosperity, the ruin of righteousness, covetous brooding, and want of wisdom — all proceed from greed.

sanskrit: anyāyaś cāvitarkaś ca vikarmasu ca yāḥ kriyāḥ kūṭavidyādayaś caiva rūpaiśvaryamadas tathā
english: Injustice and want of discernment, and those deeds done amid forbidden acts, fraudulent learning and the like, and the intoxication of beauty and dominion —

sanskrit: sarvabhūteṣv aviśvāsaḥ sarvabhūteṣv anārjavam sarvabhūteṣv abhidrohaḥ sarvabhūteṣv ayuktatā haraṇaṃ paravittānāṃ paradārābhimarśanam
english: distrust of all creatures, crookedness toward all creatures, malice toward all creatures, faithlessness toward all creatures, the seizing of others' wealth, and the violation of others' wives —

sanskrit: vāgvego mānaso vego nindāvegas tathaiva ca upasthodarayor vego mṛtyuvegaś ca dāruṇaḥ
english: the urge of speech and the urge of the mind, and likewise the urge to slander, the urge of the loins and the belly, and the dread urge that drives toward death —

sanskrit: īrṣyāvegaś ca balavān mithyāvegaś ca dustyajaḥ rasavegaś ca durvāraḥ śrotravegaś ca duḥsahaḥ
english: the mighty urge of envy, the urge to falsehood so hard to renounce, the urge of taste that none can ward off, and the urge of hearing so hard to bear —

sanskrit: kutsā vikatthā mātsaryaṃ pāpaṃ duṣkarakāritā sāhasānāṃ ca sarveṣām akāryāṇāṃ kriyās tathā
english: contempt, boastfulness, jealousy, sin, the doing of what ought not to be done, and the commission of all rash and improper deeds —

sanskrit: jātau bālye 'tha kaumāre yauvane cāpi mānavaḥ na saṃtyajaty ātmakarma yan na jīryati jīryataḥ
english: In infancy, in childhood, in boyhood, and in youth alike, man does not abandon this conduct of his own — that which does not grow old even as he grows old.

sanskrit: yo na pūrayituṃ śakyo lobhaḥ prāptyā kurūdvaha nityaṃ gambhīratoyābhir āpagābhir ivodadhiḥ na prahṛṣyati lābhair yo yaś ca kāmair na tṛpyati
english: This greed, O scion of Kuru, can never be filled by any gain, even as the ocean is never filled by ever-flowing rivers of deep waters; it rejoices not in acquisitions, and is sated by no enjoyments.

sanskrit: yo na devair na gandharvair nāsurair na mahoragaiḥ jñāyate nṛpa tattvena sarvair bhūtagaṇais tathā sa lobhaḥ saha mohena vijetavyo jitātmanā
english: That greed, which is known in its true nature, O king, neither by the gods nor by the gandharvas, nor by the asuras nor by the great serpents, nor by all the hosts of beings — that greed, together with delusion, must be conquered by one who has mastered himself.

sanskrit: dambho drohaś ca nindā ca paiśunyaṃ matsaras tathā bhavanty etāni kauravya lubdhānām akṛtātmanām
english: Hypocrisy, malice, slander, talebearing, and jealousy — these, O Kaurava, arise in the greedy whose souls are uncultivated.

sanskrit: sumahānty api śāstrāṇi dhārayanti bahuśrutāḥ chettāraḥ saṃśayānāṃ ca kliśyantīhālpabuddhayaḥ
english: The deeply learned bear in mind even the vastest treatises and resolve the doubts of others, yet here in this world the small-minded among them are tormented all the same.

sanskrit: dveṣakrodhaprasaktāś ca śiṣṭācārabahiṣkṛtāḥ antaḥkṣurā vāṅmadhurāḥ kūpāś channās tṛṇair iva dharmavaitaṃsikāḥ kṣudrā muṣṇanti dhvajino jagat
english: Given over to hatred and wrath, cast out from the conduct of the cultured, knives within yet honeyed of speech, like wells hidden over with grass, these base men, snaring the world under the banner of righteousness, plunder it.

sanskrit: kurvate ca bahūn mārgāṃs tāṃs tān hetubalāśritāḥ sarvaṃ mārgaṃ vilumpanti lobhājñāneṣu niṣṭhitāḥ
english: Relying on the force of specious reasonings, they devise many a path of their own, and so they tear up every righteous path, fixed as they are in greed and ignorance.

sanskrit: dharmasyāhriyamāṇasya lobhagrastair durātmabhiḥ yā yā vikriyate saṃsthā tataḥ sābhiprapadyate
english: When righteousness is carried off by the wicked seized with greed, whatever established order is thereby corrupted, that corruption goes on spreading from it.

sanskrit: darpaḥ krodho madaḥ svapno harṣaḥ śoko 'timānitā tata eva hi kauravya dṛśyante lubdhabuddhiṣu etān aśiṣṭān budhyasva nityaṃ lobhasamanvitān
english: Insolence, wrath, intoxication, sloth, exultation, grief, and excessive pride — these, O Kaurava, are seen for that very reason in those whose minds are greedy. Know such men to be ill-bred and forever possessed of greed.

sanskrit: śiṣṭāṃs tu paripṛcchethā yān vakṣyāmi śucivratān yeṣu vṛttibhayaṃ nāsti paralokabhayaṃ na ca
english: But of the cultured, of pure vows, whom I shall now describe to you, you should make inquiry — those in whom there is no fear concerning livelihood, nor fear concerning the next world,

sanskrit: nāmiṣeṣu prasaṅgo 'sti na priyeṣv apriyeṣu ca śiṣṭācāraḥ priyo yeṣu damo yeṣu pratiṣṭhitaḥ
english: in whom there is no clinging to sensual baits, nor to things pleasant or unpleasant, to whom the conduct of the cultured is dear, and in whom self-restraint is firmly established;

sanskrit: sukhaṃ duḥkhaṃ paraṃ yeṣāṃ satyaṃ yeṣāṃ parāyaṇam dātāro na gṛhītāro dayāvantas tathaiva ca
english: to whom the happiness and sorrow of others are their own, whose sole refuge is truth, who are givers and not takers, and who are likewise full of compassion;

sanskrit: pitṛdevātitheyāś ca nityodyuktās tathaiva ca sarvopakāriṇo dhīrāḥ sarvadharmānupālakāḥ
english: who are devoted to ancestors, gods, and guests, and ever steadfast in exertion, doers of good to all, firm of mind, and upholders of every duty;

sanskrit: sarvabhūtahitāś caiva sarvadeyāś ca bhārata na te cālayituṃ śakyā dharmavyāpārapāragāḥ
english: who seek the welfare of all beings and bestow on all, O Bhārata — such men, having reached the far shore of the practice of righteousness, cannot be swerved from their course.

sanskrit: na teṣāṃ bhidyate vṛttaṃ yat purā sādhubhiḥ kṛtam na trāsino na capalā na raudrāḥ satpathe sthitāḥ
english: The conduct laid down of old by the good is never broken in them; they are not given to terror, nor fickle, nor cruel, but stand firm upon the path of the righteous.

sanskrit: te sevyāḥ sādhubhir nityaṃ yeṣv ahiṃsā pratiṣṭhitā kāmakrodhavyapetā ye nirmamā nirahaṃkṛtāḥ suvratāḥ sthiramaryādās tān upāssva ca pṛccha ca
english: They are ever to be attended upon by the good — those in whom non-injury is firmly set, who are free from desire and wrath, free from possessiveness and from egotism, of excellent vows and steadfast bounds. Wait upon such men and question them.

sanskrit: na gavārthaṃ yaśorthaṃ vā dharmas teṣāṃ yudhiṣṭhira avaśyakārya ity eva śarīrasya kriyās tathā
english: Their righteousness, O Yudhiṣṭhira, is not for the sake of cattle nor for fame; and the offices of the body they perform only as things that must needs be done.

sanskrit: na bhayaṃ krodhacāpalyaṃ na śokas teṣu vidyate na dharmadhvajinaś caiva na guhyaṃ kiṃ cid āsthitāḥ
english: In them is found no fear, no rashness of wrath, no grief; they bear no false banner of righteousness, and they keep nothing hidden.

sanskrit: yeṣv alobhas tathāmoho ye ca satyārjave ratāḥ teṣu kaunteya rajyethā yeṣv atandrīkṛtaṃ manaḥ
english: In those in whom there is freedom from greed and delusion, who delight in truth and uprightness, in whom the mind is made free of sloth — in such men, O son of Kuntī, may you find your joy.

sanskrit: ye na hṛṣyanti lābheṣu nālābheṣu vyathanti ca nirmamā nirahaṃkārāḥ sattvasthāḥ samadarśinaḥ
english: Those who rejoice not in gains nor are troubled by their absence, who are without possessiveness, without egotism, established in goodness, and equal-eyed toward all —

sanskrit: lābhālābhau sukhaduḥkhe ca tāta; priyāpriye maraṇaṃ jīvitaṃ ca samāni yeṣāṃ sthiravikramāṇāṃ; buddhātmanāṃ sattvam avasthitānām
english: those of steadfast valour, of awakened souls, abiding in goodness, to whom gain and loss, joy and sorrow, dear friend, the pleasant and the unpleasant, death and life are all alike —

sanskrit: sukhapriyais tān sumahāpratāpān; yatto 'pramattaś ca samarthayethāḥ daivāt sarve guṇavanto bhavanti; śubhāśubhā vākpralāpā yathaiva
english: such men of mighty splendour you should, with care and watchfulness, win over by what is pleasant and agreeable; for by destiny all become endowed with their qualities, even as utterances of speech turn out good or ill.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca anarthānām adhiṣṭhānam ukto lobhaḥ pitāmaha ajñānam api vai tāta śrotum icchāmi tattvataḥ
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: Greed has been declared the seat of all calamities, O grandsire. Now of ignorance also, dear sire, I wish to hear the truth.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca karoti pāpaṃ yo 'jñānān nātmano vetti ca kṣamam pradveṣṭi sādhuvṛttāṃś ca sa lokasyaiti vācyatām
english: Bhīṣma said: He who does sin out of ignorance, who knows not what is fitting for himself, and who hates those of virtuous conduct — such a man becomes a thing of reproach in the world.

sanskrit: ajñānān nirayaṃ yāti tathājñānena durgatim ajñānāt kleśam āpnoti tathāpatsu nimajjati
english: Through ignorance a man goes to hell, and through ignorance to an evil state; through ignorance he meets with affliction, and so sinks down into calamities.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca ajñānasya pravṛttiṃ ca sthānaṃ vṛddhiṃ kṣayodayau mūlaṃ yogaṃ gatiṃ kālaṃ kāraṇaṃ hetum eva ca
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: The arising of ignorance, its seat, its growth, its decline and its increase, its root, its means, its course, its time, its occasion, and its cause —

sanskrit: śrotum icchāmi tattvena yathāvad iha pārthiva ajñānaprabhavaṃ hīdaṃ yad duḥkham upalabhyate
english: all this, O king, I wish to hear truly and just as it is; for this sorrow that is met with here springs from ignorance.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca rāgo dveṣas tathā moho harṣaḥ śoko 'bhimānitā kāmaḥ krodhaś ca darpaś ca tandrīr ālasyam eva ca
english: Bhīṣma said: Passion, hatred, and delusion, exultation, grief, and conceit, desire and wrath and insolence, drowsiness and sloth as well,

sanskrit: icchā dveṣas tathā tāpaḥ paravṛddhyupatāpitā ajñānam etan nirdiṣṭaṃ pāpānāṃ caiva yāḥ kriyāḥ
english: longing and aversion, and torment, the distress born of another's prosperity — this is declared to be ignorance, together with all the deeds of the sinful.

sanskrit: etayā yā pravṛttiś ca vṛddhyādīn yāṃś ca pṛcchasi vistareṇa mahābāho śṛṇu tac ca viśāṃ pate
english: The activity that comes of this, and the growth and the rest about which you ask — hear that too at length, O mighty-armed lord of the people.

sanskrit: ubhāv etau samaphalau samadoṣau ca bhārata ajñānaṃ cātilobhaś cāpy ekaṃ jānīhi pārthiva
english: These two, O Bhārata, are alike in their fruit and alike in their fault; ignorance and excessive greed — know them, O king, to be in truth but one.

sanskrit: lobhaprabhavam ajñānaṃ vṛddhaṃ bhūyaḥ pravardhate sthāne sthānaṃ kṣaye kṣaiṇyam upaiti vividhāṃ gatim
english: Ignorance, springing from greed, once grown waxes greater still; in stability it gains stability, in decline it meets with diminution, and so it follows many a course.

sanskrit: mūlaṃ lobhasya mahataḥ kālātmagatir eva ca chinne 'cchinne tathā lobhe kāraṇaṃ kāla eva hi
english: The root of great greed is the workings of time and of the self; whether greed be cut off or uncut, time alone is the cause thereof.

sanskrit: tasyājñānāt tu lobho hi lobhād ajñānam eva ca sarve doṣās tathā lobhāt tasmāl lobhaṃ vivarjayet
english: From its ignorance comes greed, and from greed comes ignorance again; thus all faults arise from greed, and therefore one should renounce greed.

sanskrit: janako yuvanāśvaś ca vṛṣādarbhiḥ prasenajit lobhakṣayād divaṃ prāptās tathaivānye janādhipāḥ
english: Janaka and Yuvanāśva, Vṛṣadarbhi and Prasenajit, by the destruction of greed attained heaven, and so likewise did other lords of men.

sanskrit: pratyakṣaṃ tu kuruśreṣṭha tyaja lobham ihātmanā tyaktvā lobhaṃ sukhaṃ loke pretya cānucariṣyasi
english: Plainly, then, O best of the Kurus, renounce greed here and now by your own resolve; having renounced greed, you shall dwell in happiness in this world and after death as well.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca svādhyāyakṛtayatnasya brāhmaṇasya pitāmaha dharmakāmasya dharmātman kiṃ nu śreya ihocyate
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: For a brāhmaṇa who has striven hard in the study of the Veda and who longs for righteousness, O righteous-souled grandsire, what is said to be the highest good here?

sanskrit: bahudhādarśane loke śreyo yad iha manyase asmiṃl loke pare caiva tan me brūhi pitāmaha
english: In a world where views are manifold, that which you hold to be the highest good, both in this world and in the next — that tell me, O grandsire.

sanskrit: mahān ayaṃ dharmapatho bahuśākhaś ca bhārata kiṃ svid eveha dharmāṇām anuṣṭheyatamaṃ matam
english: Great is this path of righteousness, O Bhārata, and many are its branches; which then, among all the duties, is held to be the most worthy of being practised?

sanskrit: dharmasya mahato rājan bahuśākhasya tattvataḥ yan mūlaṃ paramaṃ tāta tat sarvaṃ brūhy atandritaḥ
english: Of righteousness, O king, which is vast and many-branched, that which in truth is its supreme root — all that, dear sire, declare to me untiringly.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca hanta te kathayiṣyāmi yena śreyaḥ prapatsyase pītvāmṛtam iva prājño jñānatṛpto bhaviṣyasi
english: Bhīṣma said: Come then, I shall tell you that by which you shall attain the highest good; and like a wise man who has drunk of the nectar of immortality, you shall be sated with knowledge.

sanskrit: dharmasya vidhayo naike te te proktā maharṣibhiḥ svaṃ svaṃ vijñānam āśritya damas teṣāṃ parāyaṇam
english: The ordinances of righteousness are not few; they have been declared, this one and that, by the great seers, each relying upon his own understanding — yet self-restraint is the highest aim of them all.

sanskrit: damaṃ niḥśreyasaṃ prāhur vṛddhā niścayadarśinaḥ brāhmaṇasya viśeṣeṇa damo dharmaḥ sanātanaḥ
english: The elders, who see things with certainty, have called self-restraint the supreme good; and for a brāhmaṇa in particular self-restraint is the eternal duty.

sanskrit: nādāntasya kriyāsiddhir yathāvad upalabhyate damo dānaṃ tathā yajñān adhītaṃ cātivartate
english: For one who is unrestrained no proper accomplishment of works is found; self-restraint surpasses charity, and sacrifices, and the study of the Veda.

sanskrit: damas tejo vardhayati pavitraṃ ca damaḥ param vipāpmā tejasā yuktaḥ puruṣo vindate mahat
english: Self-restraint increases a man's spiritual energy; self-restraint is the supreme purifier; and the man who is free from sin and endowed with such energy attains the great goal.

sanskrit: damena sadṛśaṃ dharmaṃ nānyaṃ lokeṣu śuśruma damo hi paramo loke praśastaḥ sarvadharmiṇām
english: We have heard of no other duty in the worlds that is the equal of self-restraint; for self-restraint is the supreme thing in the world, praised by all who follow righteousness.

sanskrit: pretya cāpi manuṣyendra paramaṃ vindate sukham damena hi samāyukto mahāntaṃ dharmam aśnute
english: And after death too, O lord of men, the self-restrained man attains supreme happiness; for joined with self-restraint he wins to the great reward of righteousness.

sanskrit: sukhaṃ dāntaḥ prasvapiti sukhaṃ ca pratibudhyate sukhaṃ paryeti lokāṃś ca manaś cāsya prasīdati
english: The self-restrained man sleeps in happiness and in happiness awakes; in happiness he ranges through the worlds, and his mind is serene.

sanskrit: adāntaḥ puruṣaḥ kleśam abhīkṣṇaṃ pratipadyate anarthāṃś ca bahūn anyān prasṛjaty ātmadoṣajān
english: The unrestrained man meets again and again with affliction, and brings upon himself many other calamities born of his own faults.

sanskrit: āśrameṣu caturṣv āhur damam evottamaṃ vratam tasya liṅgāni vakṣyāmi yeṣāṃ samudayo damaḥ
english: In all the four stages of life they call self-restraint the highest vow; and I shall declare its marks, whose sum and union is self-restraint.

sanskrit: kṣamā dhṛtir ahiṃsā ca samatā satyam ārjavam indriyāvajayo dākṣyaṃ mārdavaṃ hrīr acāpalam
english: Forbearance, steadfastness, non-injury, evenness of mind, truth, uprightness, mastery over the senses, skill, gentleness, modesty, and freedom from fickleness;

sanskrit: akārpaṇyam asaṃrambhaḥ saṃtoṣaḥ priyavāditā avivitsānasūyā cāpy eṣāṃ samudayo damaḥ
english: absence of meanness, freedom from agitation, contentment, kindly speech, freedom from craving, and freedom from spite — the union of all these is self-restraint.

sanskrit: gurupūjā ca kauravya dayā bhūteṣv apaiśunam janavādo 'mṛṣāvādaḥ stutinindāvivarjanam
english: Reverence for elders, O Kaurava, compassion toward all beings, freedom from talebearing, courteous discourse, truthful speech, and the shunning alike of flattery and of slander —

sanskrit: kāmaḥ krodhaś ca lobhaś ca darpaḥ stambho vikatthanam moha īrṣyāvamānaś cety etad dānto na sevate
english: desire and wrath and greed, insolence, stubborn pride, and boastfulness, delusion, envy, and contempt — these the self-restrained man does not indulge.

sanskrit: anindito hy akāmātmāthālpeccho 'thānasūyakaḥ samudrakalpaḥ sa naro na kadā cana pūryate
english: Blameless, free of desire in soul, of few wants, and untouched by spite — such a man is like the ocean, and is never to be filled.

sanskrit: ahaṃ tvayi mama tvaṃ ca mayi te teṣu cāpy aham pūrvasaṃbandhisaṃyogān naitad dānto niṣevate
english: "I am yours, and you are mine; you are theirs, and I am theirs" — such attachments, born of former bonds of kinship and union, the self-restrained man does not cherish.

sanskrit: sarvā grāmyās tathāraṇyā yāś ca loke pravṛttayaḥ nindāṃ caiva praśaṃsāṃ ca yo nāśrayati mucyate
english: All the pursuits of the world, whether of the village or of the forest, and likewise both blame and praise — he who clings to none of these is set free.
